thread:
erica: Heads-up — rolled keystore RBAC split at 02:10 UTC and we started seeing mTLS handshake rejects from NA edge clusters. Proxy 502 spikes and on the backend we see 'handshake denied'. Anyone oncall?

sam: I see a blip on the perf dashboard. Which principal is being denied?

erica: svc-proxy when it calls keystore to unwrap TLS keys. Sample keystore log: 
```
2026-08-12T02:14:23Z keystore-1 INFO rbac-check: principal=svc-proxy.na check=decrypt result=DENY reason=subject-not-present
2026-08-12T02:14:23Z proxy-7 WARN tls: handshake failed client=svc-api.na, err=handshake_denied stage=unwrap-key
```

priya: If keystore does early-authorize it may return DENY without calling KMS which explains empty KMS audit. Can you confirm KMS audit for decrypts from svc-proxy.na?

erica: verified — no KMS decrypt entries. I also checked kube-audit: the RoleBinding apply shows the new binding, but the subjects array is missing the serviceaccount for the NA cluster. Looks like a templating edge-case.

ops-oncall: I can hotfix the RoleBinding in na-prod. Before doing that let's capture forensic artifacts: full keystore pod logs, proxy sidecar logs (grep peer_cert_sha256 and sni), kube-audit event for the RoleBinding apply, and the rendered manifest that CI applied.

erica: commands I'm running to gather: 
```
kubectl -n infra --context=na-prod get rolebinding keystore-svc -o yaml > /tmp/rb.yaml
kubectl -n services logs proxy-7 --since=20m | grep peer_cert_sha256 | head -n 5
curl "https://console.internal/kms/audit?principal=svc-proxy.na&op=Decrypt&since=1h"
```

ops-oncall: Rolling the binding patch now: 
```
kubectl --context=na-prod -n infra apply -f /manifests/keystore/rolebinding-add-sas-na.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore -n infra
```

keystore-bot: Created trace id trace-keystore-na-20260812 for correlating keystore logs and audit stubs.

~6 minutes later~

erica: After patch and restart, handshake rejects dropped from 3.6% -> 0.2% in NA. Services recovered.

sam: Good. Post-incident follow-ups: 1) fix the RBAC template to always emit fully-qualified serviceaccount subjects per-cluster (don't rely on group expansion), 2) add a pipeline preflight that runs a canary decrypt as the target SA in-cluster post-apply, 3) change keystore so that when it returns early DENY it also emits a small "audit_stub" event to our logshipper with fields principal, reason, sni, peer_cert_sha256, and trace_id.

priya: I'll handle audit retention and sink config so audit_stub events are preserved and queryable. We should set KMS/audit retention to 90 days for decrypt-related events and ensure logshipper indexes audit_stub entries with the same trace id.

ops-oncall: Also propose adding metric keystore_rbac_early_deny_total{region} and a paging alert if rate > 0.5% for 3m. Runbook steps: 1) `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-* -o yaml`, 2) `kubectl logs deploy/keystore -n infra | grep rbac-check`, 3) check KMS audit for Decrypt entries and audit-stub events in logshipper.

erica: I'll open a PR that fixes the template and adds the canary decrypt job. Assigning: erica -> RBAC template PR and rollout plan, sam -> canary job + CI gate, priya -> audit sink and retention, ops-oncall -> alert + runbook update, keystore-bot -> change to emit audit_stub behind feature flag.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-410 created: "NA mTLS handshake rejects after keystore RBAC split". PagerDuty notified. Please attach incident timeline and artifact links to the PR.

erica: Thanks all. We'll run a short blameless postmortem focusing on pipeline templating and preflight gaps. One additional ask: add a pre-deploy invariant check in the rotation job to fail if rendered RoleBinding subjects do not include the expected SAs for each target cluster.

sam: also add a canary rollout pattern: apply RBAC change to a single canary cluster, run canary-decrypt, and only then roll global. Avoid all-at-once group swaps.

keystore-bot: Note: planned release will add structured fields `audit_stub_id`, `rbac_eval_trace`, and `keystore_cache_hit` to logs so incidents don't lose context. Feature behind flag `keystore.emit_earlydeny_audit`.

erica: closing the loop here — recovery confirmed and follow-ups tracked in the incident board. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
